It’s empowering.
The control.
The taking over.
The ability to remove yourself. Think. Breathe.

It’s an ability. A superpower.
To love. Deep enough it debilitates. Turns the world into a dream. A nightmare. A rollercoaster.

It’s a blessing. To live. Be alive, take chances. Run until your lungs give in. No matter what. You run.

A zen. To breathe slow… like a dance you shy away from. With yourself… pacing, every step counted… until you become one.

You are superhuman. Able to move it all with emotion. Obstacles. Floods. Earthquakes. Eruptions of the deadly kind.

We are… one. Whether you run, miles. Whether you stay, hours. Whether you avoid, days.

I am here. Living. Reliving.
The world crumbling around me, sickness taking over my body. It’s criminal…

No matter.
We are royalty.
 We are magical.
We are terrestrial.
We are universal.

Likely.

Dear Let’s-Call-You-Jack,

The rain fell over San Francisco last night and all I keep thinking about is how I wasn’t anywhere near San Fran to enjoy it. You know how much I love the rain.
The days are getting colder and I swear I can see my exhaling breath exhausted in the air.

I miss you. If I am honest, I don’t understand what is happening. I live my life so everlastingly different to yours; the concept of ever giving up a piece of euphoria so great, so true, and so purely honest doesn’t reach my neurons enough to compute. To choose to let go of a person who at your core and bones you know, would never betray you, would always be there for you and forever love you. In a world of so much fakery, so much disloyalty and deception, your decisions keep surprising me at every turn.

The unfortunate part of this beautifully painful life, is that it is not everlasting. It ends just as quickly as it began. We plan our futures like headless chickens running around an empty garden of hope, long enough to finally experience that final blackout. And in between that time? We feel pain. We feel pain because of all the things we don’t have. We forget we only have today. The opportunities, friends, and loved ones dancing around us, reaching out to us, are but a mere tease for all the things we dont have; until you maybe find what you think you were looking for only to realize how much time you wasted not being with the ones you truly wanted.

A wise man once told me - Never waste time visiting me at my grave. I won’t hear you then. Spend time with me now, when I am alive and can be here with you. Do not live your life in the regrets of time wasted. Live your life in the bliss of the insane chances you took that made you feel alive.

I hope you are living blissfully with your decisions now. That life is how you imagined it would be. I hope you are surrounded by love, and by friends you can lean on. I hope you are happier swimming in your overwhelming thoughts, planning your currently nonexistent future, than living in the now with me.

May you have no regrets.

Sincerely always and forever,
Let’s-Call-Me-Jane

Some days, it’s hard to breathe.
I thought, maybe, you were one in a million.
But the scars I have, I can’t alter.
And now all I gave you, is lost. Thrown into a fast flowing river, never to be seen again.
It all drowned, just as quickly as I learned to breathe.
Again.
With you, I thought I built something that we couldn’t shake. Something forever wouldn’t break down.
During my last breath, I kept fighting, kept swimming, kept trying, kept wanting.
But you pushed my head underwater one last time and watched me finally die.

I’m an astronaut with a tear in my suit. My tears flow through it, turning them into ice with every breath I exhale.
The silence here isn’t silent at all as I float in zero gravity to bring back my spirits I lost somewhere among the exhaustion and hope.

Moving with not nearly the speed of light but close enough that my body feels enough adrenaline to float without guilt. It boils inside me like a yellow submarine submerged in my ears sending sound waves to my brain as we sail on to the sun.

I am captain of this ship. Commander of a crew singing into the void of an empty vessel pulling us into an oblivion that’s elongated by our tragic laughter.

It’s ok, they said.
You did all you could, they said.
The best you could, they said.

I’m a woman with a tear in my skirt. My tears falling onto the pavement, turning crystal with every breath I inhale.
The noise here is deafening as the gravity pulls me down further towards my raving despair.​

We are out there somewhere.
We abandoned ship.

I shut my eyes to an empty casket staring back at me, hands pressed firmly onto foreheads of people, in the town where I was born.

You are inside my everyday now. No matter how many times I push you towards the edge, you’ve entangled your tentacles into my nervous system like a disease ready to eat me from the inside.

I’m flowing down a waterfall into hell’s kitchen where the steaks are a little too well done for my taste but they still taste so good I don’t mind, hell.

You look at me, raising my pulse to heights I’ve been missingly craving, and yet we move with a flow that’s been leaving stainless bedsheets in its wake.

Let’s be honest, we’ve been following every impulse right down to the last drop of gin tonic, then refiling our glasses without the necessary breath, suffocating our realities.

Nothing we can’t control apparently, until we trip back into each others’ presence, like a fungal infection controlling our brains, leading us somewhere it can flourish until it kills us.

The damage left by the wreckage of an attempted affair in-fueled by honest attraction, chemicals dancing in front of our noses, nothing but empty words and misplaced trust that’s left to ponder the days we used to say;

Friends forever, right?

I’m a garbage disposal for your semen wrapped in bits of cookie cut love. A French exposé of a life once ripped in the center of a bulletproof induced heart.

A bench made out of empty parquet floorboard on top of my fridge where I sit alone staring at my empty home.

At least I’m cute, the glitter suffocating the crimson soled heels I never wear as my everyday fashion statement.

At least I’m loud, colored in yellow horns inside a firestorm enwrapping me in the arms of a lion.

At least I’m bold, the Adobe font smudged on my face dripping into my mascara just enough it never dries out the tears.

Try and stop me; get me.

I hide inside restaurants serving red wine running through my veins, a mirage at the center of a white lie.
They call me names I don’t understand but relate to.
Inside the deepened holes of your penetration my walls scar just enough to feel joy.

The clock is ticking like a woodpecker burring a hole in my skull. Four hours left to go and I am nowhere near the space in time I want to reside in. Two years a waste of nothing but a good bourbon on my shelf, leaving me with scars I never thought possible.

We are in this together, aging. 10, 20, 30… Going on 60 soon enough to be caught under a wave of past experiences that should have happened, yet never did. Regret, an enemy of the soul, leaving it empty just enough you want to fill it with your future. The present never seems to fit into this equation.

It all fades eventually though. The sun does rise, the moments do come, and those blip few seconds where your eyelashes collide in a blink, make you just another moment wiser.

A shared timeline of breaths taken makes us human, so I say let's continue breathing till death do us part.

I glow in the dark when the world that's wrapped around me suffocates me into oblivion once or twice. Closed eyelids don't help the odd oozy liquid escaping the corners of my eyes. I wish it was a different feeling, maybe a little less sharp when I breathe in, but the stabbing pain persists into nightfall when the shadows are already asleep. A sudden feel of failure enwraps my rays bouncing off the walls of the room; my life a night club with VIP attendance. A troubling feeling I am familiar with, almost like a friend that comes to visit just to make sure I'm not ok and can lend a superficial helping hand.

I glow in the dark when the screaming isn't loud enough to pierce my dogs ears who sleeps soundly through the jackhammers in my head. My vocal cords wounded from the alcohol hitting everything but my bloodstream, slowly killing my familiar insanity. I hear nothing but thumping that self regulates at an irregular speed inside my chest. My rosy complexion turns snow white and nothing but my seven bottles of wine dig in my mind when home from work I go.

I glow in the dark when the sun finally comes out but I am still stuck in the closet. These clothes aren't mine, my brain slipping into a dream-like cocktail of bourgeois puppets being pulled in all directions by a master who can't make up their mind. A theatrical failure on an empty stage with a full audience to judge an undeveloped form of art.

It's just that time of the month.

They call me boring most days.
They might be right. I don't like getting out the house much. Forced chains around my neck pulling me toward hells basement, I paint the perfect picket fence picturesque house wife. My skirt just short enough to be fun, long enough to be appropriate, and colored all sorts of cupcake fun. I wear heels, not too high, not to thin, boring colored, toes bubble gum pink. Hair pulled back, but not too tight, that would be too confident. Husband's out most days, the kids a load I carry with a smile. Love the little mistakes I've made running around my kitchen.

Then night falls. House cleaned, husbands lover keeping him busy, kids snoring like chainsaws, and the lights dimmed to the perfect magazine shade of poise.
My heels come off, skirt neatly folded on the dryer, my underwear color matched with the bottle of red I keep in the fridge. I like mine cold and poisonous.
Music's on, TV's off. Im dancing in a glittered sprinkled slimy dreamlike state all the way to the pool. I jump in.

"Wake up!"

Hungover. Single. Naked.

Welcome to the good life.

I fell asleep. Again. All I remember is yelling and the couch in my face. Rough night.

He isn't here. I wonder why. Maybe he needed space. Or maybe he isn't coming back.

My dog is hungry. His bowl is filled with a bottle of rum I spilled. He doesn't seem to want it. Allow me then.

Where are my cigarettes? The only things I ever constantly lose and always need. Fuck.

Who's she? Hello? I guess she stayed the night. I don't speak German. Excuse me.

The kitchen's a mess. I'm ignoring it. Need coffee. Stepping over leftover food on the floor. Swell.

Stepped on broken glass. The pain is nice. Good morning, sun-shiny day. Where did I put down that dog bowl?

He's back. Kissed me. Kissed her. She definitely slept here last night. Good.

Who is he? I don't know you. She at least feels familiar. Coffee tastes good right now. Lighter please.

I'm not wearing underwear. My bra is too tight. This is uncomfortable.

Sure, you can have one. I should light it for her too. She speaks my language. I like her lips.

The silence is awkward. Should I say something to break this stance of shame?

She kissed me. Hm. I'll kiss her back. She feels known. I've been here before. He's back. I'm home.

Let me tell you a story about Mr. Eeky-Weeky and his uncanny ability to make things out of fuzz.

He was a small thing, that Mr. Eeky-Weeky, yet charming as can be. A little push is all it took for Mr. Eeky-Weeky to rise above his humdrum job to his multi-billion business named Fuzz It All.

Let's go back a little though, to a place where he once needed. A place real small, where he was born, not that tall, but he called it home.

"Fresh baked cookies and a coffee pot, the smell of fresh croissants. Not quite a breakfast of champions, but close enough", he thought.

On one sunny day, as breakfast came and went, he thought "I think the day's too clear!" He jumped up high, with a half impressed smile, then sat back down to think. "I think, I think" but nothing came. He thought again, "I think, I think," and still the same. His brain a door that wouldn't open, even for the best of his mindful voices.

Another day would come and go until 100 days later, he finally spoke:

"A day too clear needs a fuzzy reinvention, an unconventional decor. It needs the sound of fuzz to ring soundtracks at passersbys, playing music at romantic restaurants. It needs curly dresses that twirl beneath the seams at the hips, fuzzy love on the skins of those who wear it.

It needs an oil painting across the river created by a master, capturing the fuzzy houses in the reflection of the water as the photos taken of the passing cars capture forever the insanity of speed with a fuzz-like exposure."

A fuzzy idea. Not very polished, but enough, he thought, to make a leash for puppy Olie he loved too much for words to... "Ah, I lost it."

He leaned down to find the wind was blowing from underneath the table he was hard at working. And there he saw it, a pile of fuzz from little Olie, whose time for shedding was prime in its glory.

And there it started and there it went. A leash, a collar, and soon a dress, for fuzz had no limits to address. He worked and worked on laces, and hats, and on many things until, at last, he tailored a beautiful coat that made its way to runways, fashionistas, and headlines. Mr. Eeky-Weeky became a sensation overnight, and he soon became the fashion icon of Milan; the world cheered at all his creations, and only the rich could afford his chic.

His world did change like he had wanted and the clear days in the sun finally ended up fuzzy.

I have a cry wolf taped shut in a shoe box under the fridge. It likes to be in a cooler environment so it can complain about it.

I often times wonder if I should throw it out, but the thought of separation gives me anxiety. It has me where it wants me.

Sometimes it screams and scares the neighbours. Other times, it sits in silence, unnoticed. I often times wonder if I should call for help when it gets angry, but it quickly calms itself into remission.

It's been a challenge living under the same roof together. I am not one for sudden loud noises; they make my heart skip an unhealthy number of beats. Not knowing when or why it might have an episode puts me on permanent emotional standby.

We've lived together for years. I don't remember my life without it, although on occasion some flashes of my past resurface at the most inconvenient times. I shut them out altogether. It can sense when I'm reminiscing, and I try not to draw unnecessary attention.

My friends keep asking if there is anything they can do to help, but that question really bores me. Courtesy mannerisms are pointless. One might as well keep to their own business instead of draining the little life I have left with such shit.

The box got broken into last night. The clues say my rat infestation might have finally got the best of us. My cables also took quite a hit, so watching television might require some additional effort. It sucks, too, because I was really getting into this show.

I now have a rat in a cage on my fridge, with a cry wolf in its belly.

I watch him standing there screwing it in with this look of complexity. I'm laying on my back in bed, my hair hanging off the side, soaking in the water I spilled on the floor while trying to cure my hangover.

The dog is asleep beside me, probably dreaming about last night and the champagne he licked off the floor after the countdown.

New Year's Eve has always been a complicated rollercoaster of emotions, mostly pertaining to the accomplishments the year helped me achieve.

This year however, felt like more of a collective feeling, as if the world stood still, taking in the last breath that 2020 had to offer amongst all the disasters it had already put us through. All waiting for the countdown to end, so we can begin into what some might see as a fresh start.

We are now in 2021. It feels like electing a new president that will either continue destroying its country, or slowly mend it again through drips and bandages. No one knows, and we all wait for the screw to either hold it all in or break.

I keep watching him work as my dog snores away the last drop of that 2020 champagne.

It was this time of year that the pot was boiling on my stove with a raspberry smell and a hint of chocolate. I wanted to believe it was done so I could taste it, but it seems a watched pot really never finishes. Neither did I that night.

It was a perfect. I got everything ready, I was prepared. An unfair life, but a fool consumed by obsession is just that, a fool. You stepped through my door like the perfect statue you were, an unfortunately emotionless specimen with perfect muscles. I felt lucky, a fox in her prime easily catching prey she can play with for a while. A fun thought, a sad reality.

I was barely able to serve you the drink I so carefully made. Your clothes were already being ripped to the floor with such an unfortunate desire. Two should have played your game that night.

Your lips were a stale, cracked imagination of the Sahara Desert, lonely, confused, and so tastelessly bare. My clothes still on while you stood there so vulnerably naked didn't give me the power I desired. It just made you look weak.

The man in my room I had wanted to fuck was now not intriguing enough to me to be fun. It was a strange realization that your beautifully carved body was never going to be enough to make a woman satisfied.

You tried. A kiss on the neck, a nibble on the ear. All the typical things one would do on a first date. Not quite my thing. Like the dripping water from a fountain I was not.

When you left, I sat waiting for a chance to shake the strangeness I felt when you touched me, a distanced feeling from a man too near for me to bare. Let me be clearer, I hated everything you were and all you continue to represent.

And yet I continue to masturbate to your memory.

I am terrified of dying. So much so, anything related to death puts me in a lump sum of legs and arms shoved in a corner facing just enough wall to feel safe. I hate it.

It all started when my aunt died in her sleep due to a brain aneurysm. Wrapping my head around the thought that you can kiss someone goodnight, never to wake up to them again is close to… "Um, no".

The fear is probably a useless one, especially because I can't control death. And yet, I find myself in tears picturing when death will come. We go through life thinking it's the enemy that ends all, takes away the you, leaves behind the remains you have no control of, and smirks at the hope that your family might have actually read the letter attached to your will and scattered you over Mount Kilimanjaro like you've always dreamed of. We reconcile with it through preparations: life insurances, wills, savings accounts, hoping to leave behind a safe haven for our loved ones.

Somewhere in this cluster of vast fear and precaution, I have forgotten I am currently very much alive - locked up in my house so that others can also have a fighting chance at life. There's a sense of unity with the world as I sit here trying to remember what my friends used to look like.

I think it must be a life lesson of some sort.

Even when I do get in touch with friends, I have a hard time catching them up. It's like a ping pong game of "How are yous?" and "What's news?", both sides feeling a lack of conversation that used to be so natural. How do you talk about the internal growth, the pain, the struggles, and the setbacks when they are all brand new to you? I sometimes don't even recognise myself through this new lens of isolation. It was easier when I could talk about my awful trips to London, or my first hangover at a gay bar where I met one of my best friends, or any story about something that actually happened.

I often think about how our generation will go down in history.

Our grandparents went to war, telling us stories of their battles. What will we tell our grandkids? That we complained about being stuck inside for a few months while the clubs shut down? That we laughed at people in power until they made us cry? That we took too long to fight for equality until one too many people died? We might just need to tell them that we were always a step behind, but always had the right intentions.

I am terrified of dying because I don't know how our story will be told.

I end up on this hill a lot, looking down at the people whose lives continue to pass by while mine runs still, a sad irony that is not lost on me. The houses look like a miniature architectural mockup; the people just working ants, busy doing their jobs.

Mary is probably still tending to her chocolate shop, working until those late hours of the night like she used to, so that when the morning comes her customers can buy her freshly made goodies. They really are something special.

John, her husband, is behind the counter counting the money they earned that day hoping it will be enough to pay back the unhappy customer that dropped the freshly baked chocolate cake Mary spent all day making.

Tina keeps singing at the bar across town knowing one day she will make it big. The crowd keeps throwing drinks at her but her commitment to her art is bigger than a few wet see-through T-shirts as her breasts illuminate the stage.

Katherine jogs every morning and swims in her private pool every night. She has never understood the struggles of life or that you need to work to attain materialistic things or experiences. Money has never been a problem for her. That is, what many would call, "pure fucking luck".

Timmy keeps disappearing for days and then appearing at the worst times. Being one of the only teenagers in town is hard for him, because he just doesn't quite fit in. The world is just too unfair for him right now and he has trouble handling it.

Everyone forgot about my death last week though. I was taking a stroll down to the corner store where Bob works, just to get a few snacks. I saw Jeffy stuck in a tree across the street and thought what a shame it must be to cry for help with no one listening. I thought the cat deserved a break, and since the local firefighters were busy saving Cindy's life across town from a burning building, I decided to cross the street. A poor decision on my part, especially given the fact I forgot the basic rule taught to us all as children: always look left first.

Poor Jeffy; I hope he made it down.

This is what the routine looks like: he goes to work for about two weeks, is gone for one, and then spends the next few days in the hospital. Not what one would call the best life. I would like to feel sorry for the guy, but he does it to himself which is the worst part. Why would you want to live a life like that?

Jack is one of the many people that fail at committing suicide. He isn't generally depressed either, but when a moment of true passion hits, and that passion mixes with that severe emptiness, he just has to go for the knife.

You'd think he'd learn by now that killing yourself just isn't that simple. It takes a lot to off yourself, and most people fail because they just don't do it well enough; and thank God for that. Hospitals get tired of those teenagers short of a few pills that decided their first breakup was just too much to continue living.

Not Jack though, he takes his tragedies to a whole other level. Jack likes to bleed publicly. All over the grocery stores, all over the parking lot, and once, all over a wedding dress. He wants people to watch, to pay attention, and ultimately, wants to live. This fascinating mental cycle of Jack's has him landing in the hospital monthly; the surgeon knows him by name.

One month however, Jack decided to stop. What's interesting about that is we all came to ask ourselves "What's wrong with Jack this month?" like it was somehow normal that cutting his wrists was the norm, and not doing so made him crazy.

The reason for this break was a girl; beautiful, tall, and blue eyed. He had fallen hard. She was European, with a heavy German accent and gorgeous blonde hair. On the outside, she was his perfection, a perfect piece for his puzzle mind.

One day however, Natasha did succeed where so many fail. She left without even a note to explain why. She was serious about it. She just wanted to be gone. Her attempt was successful because she chose a method that could never fail; she drove up a mountain and flew off the other side. Clean break.

Jack grieved for weeks. One month passed by, two months passed by, and after three years of not attempting anything, I just had to know.

"Hey Jack, why'd you stop?" I asked.

"Got bored." he said.

I had to double check that I had heard right. "You got bored?"

"Yeah."

I didn't know what to respond to that. His answer took me by surprise.
"Why do you ask?" he said.

"Honestly, because everyone in town is wondering; they just don't have the guts to ask." I said.

"That's the thing about people, they spend so much unnecessary time asking themselves questions that have no answer. What a waste of life." he said.

"So it really is that simple then, huh? You just got bored?" I said.

"Exactly."

To this day I still wonder how the answer could have been so simple. With so much heartache, I somehow wanted the answer to be deeper, more painful; for my entertainment, so that I could have had a story to tell everyone and be the center of attention. I wanted that high, the rush of knowing what others didn't, and being the first to find out.

I wonder if part of him knew that.

I'm obsessed with you. Wherever you go, whatever you do, I want you. I know your weaknesses, things that scare you, how to get under your skin. When I watch you undress in front of your window it feels like you want people to watch; or do you want me to watch? I don't like hearing about the ones that came before me and got a taste of you, but if I don't listen to what you say, how will I ever match them, be better than them, beat them at their game? You text me when you have hard times, I come pick you back up, and then you fuck them instead of me.

This new toy you take into your bed is scum, did you know that? A shit lawyer that puts good people behind bars just to make a little bit more money at the end of the day. Your taste in toys leaves something to be desired, darling.

I'm tired of sleeping in my car just to make sure you are alright. If you just chose me instead of them, things would be so much easier, relaxing, loving. We could be together, and I could keep you safe. Being in love with you is driving me insane. I know you find safety with me, company, because you know me. I'm familiar. Is that why you don't want me, because there just isn't enough mystery to keep you interested? How the fuck am I supposed to change that?

Morning comes and there goes the lawyer, walking out of your apartment without a care in world. Another day hard at work while you wash off your night endeavors under a cold shower with some morning whiskey. You are beautiful, perfect in fact, and I stand in front of your window picturing myself under that stream of water with you.

Starting with some light kisses on your neck and working my way down to your back, I spin you around and work my way back up to your collarbone. Slowly taking off your clothes I make sure the bathroom steams up just right, ditching that cold shower you think you want. I would make you mine better than others ever have, I can promise you that.

You were supposed to warn me before you cut so deep into my soul, love. I wasn't prepared, and I don't appreciate that. Maybe when they come looking for us, they will understand how unfair you've been. I don't expect you to understand me. I don't expect you to want to. I don't love her; you should know that. She is a replacement for the pain you caused. For the emptiness I feel because you never saw me, you never wanted me, you just never fucking cared. So, when you find us, think of me for one of your shitty selfish seconds, because I know I would have been the best you've ever had.

How much do you think that this house is worth? Just look at these doors, they must cost thousands. My truck is outside in the sun, and I know once I come back those seats are going to be boiling. I hate my job; I have no idea how I ended up here. This box is extremely heavy, but I am hesitating to put it down for some reason. The house just feels odd to me, and there's no one home. What if someone steals this, then it's going to be my fault for not being careful enough. I should probably check around the house to see if there might be another spot I can put this.

All of the doors seem closed and I am still carrying this heavy thing. What's in here anyway? I need to put this down for a second, my hands are about to give in. I know this house, I deliver their mail every day and yet somehow today it just feels oddly quiet. Someone is always home, and most of the time what I assume are the husband and wife argue loudly. It's always about really boring stuff, like where the silverware goes, and how he needs to rinse the dishes before her puts them in the dishwasher. It's really much too quiet today.

My car is heating up and I left my door open which is going to be an extra blow. I hate my work in the summer, especially because I always have to have my windows down so it never cools off. I feel like I have been standing here awkwardly for the last ten minutes. Why can't I just leave? I think I should open the front door. Well, it's unlocked. Oh no, what do I do now? Now I definitely can't leave, they forgot to lock their door. I need to stay here to guard the house.

It's getting really hot out here. It feels really cool in there. I shouldn't go in though, that would be an invasion of privacy. Or would it be, if I am only doing it for selfless reasons? I am after all, just protecting them. Alright, I'm going in, but I am just going to sit on the couch until I feel like it is safe to leave.

Oh no, I must have dozed off. What's the time? Do I hear them coming? I need to get out of here fast.

"Honey, why is the mailman's car here?" asks the wife.

"Not sure, it seems to still be running. How strange."

"Do you see him anywhere?"

"I don't think so. Wasn't Annie's package supposed to arrive today?" he says.

"That's what she told me."

I hear them approaching the house. Hiding in the bathroom was not the most clever idea. I should have just unlocked one of the other eight doors in the house and ran. I am so stupid.

"Did you forget to lock the door?" she says.

"That's the third time that happened to me. I'm sorry honey, maybe it's time I finally see that doctor you recommended."

They are inside the house now. I can't go anywhere, I'm officially stuck here.

"Honey, is this the package?" she asks.

"How on earth did this get inside?" he asks.

"Maybe it came this morning and you forgot about it? It wouldn't be the first time, you know. We really should get you checked." she says.

I need to get out of here before they realize I'm here.

"I will be right back to help with those groceries, just going to the bathroom." she says.

Well, now I'm screwed.

I hide into their bathroom closet. I can barely fit in here. What's that smell? Please let this be over soon, I can't breathe in here. I can hear her coming into the bathroom, door is opening and closing, the sink turns on, and the shower? Is she taking a shower? What the fuck is happening, I can't stay here for…

"So, do you want to come out or should I make you come out?"

Fuck. Who is she talking to? Is she on the phone?

"I won't ask twice."

I need to stay perfectly still. Don't breathe. Don't move.

She opens the closet.

I've been kicking this stupid pebble for over 5 minutes, and I probably moved an inch. School's out and I need to be walking home to meet my parents for lunch, but I just can't seem to get myself moving. They just haven't been my safe space lately, and I feel like I'm going through a lot of shit. I'm often misunderstood and when I try to be polite and nice, I am just seen as selfish. Such is a day in the life of a teenager.

My days are overwhelmed by thoughts of failure. I'm not doing enough at home, my grades aren't what my parents want them to be, I don't have any raw talents for art or music, and most of all, I can't seem to get myself motivated enough to accomplish much. Not the best.

I have a boyfriend who is into playing video games, so when we aren't in school I don't really see him much. I tried to get into the world of consoles and controllers, but it really doesn't interest me. So aside from making out in the hallway and pissing off our teachers, there is not much there in the love department of moi.

My sense of style is very somber. Mostly dark greys and blacks. I don't like to showcase myself in front of people or give them any reason to judge me; I do that enough myself. Honesty is something I value above all else, so if I catch you in lie you have probably lost my trust forever. This little quirk of mine burned itself into my brain after I walked in on my mother having sex with a man that was not my father when I was 7. He had lived 50 years in this house, yet he was standing in an unfamiliar hallway. He wondered why the paintings that hung on the walls felt so foreign, and why the lights were dimmer than he had preferred them.

"Dementia had finally gotten the better of me." he thought, but then quickly remembered he was never actually diagnosed with it.

"I guess that would be too easy of an answer."

Walking down the freshly stretched out carpet, the air seemed to be getting thinner, and the door that used to lead down to the basement was no longer there.

"That's strange." he thought.

Continuing to walk down the hallway, feeling as if it was never ending, it all felt more and more like a dream. For a moment it seemed almost as if the walls moved around him while he stood still. He knew it wasn't a dream though, it felt more real than that.

"Strange… that painting's new. I don't remember hanging it there. It's quite ugly." he said.

"I hung it there." said a voice. "I think it looks nice. It fits with the rest of the ensemble."

He turned around to see who was talking to him, but no one was there. Confused he stopped in his tracks, but the walls continued to move. Beethoven's 5th Symphony started to play in the background, and soon it consumed the entire hallway. Lights started to slowly brighten as the music approached its crescendo, and the air around him got colder, leaving him shivering where he stood.

Everything went dark for a moment.

"Keep talking to him. He can hear you." said a voice.

"Hello?" he said.

The voices were muffled, but he could hear more people joining in. They sounded familiar, he just couldn't quite make out who they were or what they were saying.

"Hello? Can you hear me?" he said.

The music was so loud now the only way to be heard through it was by screaming.

"Hey! I'm right here! Can you hear me?" he yelled.

The lights turned back on and started to get brighter, as if a rocket ship approaching the sun. It was unbearable to keep his eyes open, so he tried covering them with his hands. One of the lightbulbs in front of him exploded, then another one, a third one, one after the other. The darkness crept towards him leaving him no choice but to turn and run the other way from where he presumably came from.

"Help! Help me!" he yelled.

The music rose to a thunderous volume, the darkness creeping behind him seemed unstoppable, and just as he was about to stop running, he noticed the walls stood still again. The painting he'd never seen before hung stationary beside him as he continued to run, the floor of the hallway moving faster, like a treadmill.

Then it all stopped.

For a second, he could breathe again. That's all he needed. The music shut off, the air got warmer, and the lights on his side of the hallways dimmed again.

"I'm not sure how long. It could be years. I'm so sorry." he heard them talking.

"Hello?" he called out.

"They can't hear you." said the voice.

"Who are you?"

"I'm you. The part of you still out there somewhere. I'm here to stay though, if you need me; misery loves company, and I have a feeling we might be stuck here for a while. We had quite the accident."

"I don't understand. Am I dead?" he said.

"No, but we're not living either."

"So, what do I do now?"

"We start walking. The door we need is at the end of the hallway."

With a serene sad confusion, he started to walk.

"Not that way. The other way."

He turned around to face the darkness. It's at that moment that he realized where he was, why he was, and what his chances were of finding that door. He stopped to stare at the nothingness that used to be him. The memories that hung on his walls, the lights that used to illuminate his path, and the soundtrack to his life, all gone. A part of his core self, just a dark hole in his brain.

"I think I'll just sit here and appreciate this painting you hung for a while. Come join me." he said.

"This is a nightmare. For sure. What else could it be? I feel like every sign points to it."

"This is a dream. I know it. Nothing can possibly be this good. It's nothing like anything I've ever experienced."

"This is reality. An in-between of love and hate, crime and heroism, disaster and creation. Everything and nothing happens here."

"This is the universe. A bigger you, a never ending me, and the infinite possibility of ultimate chaos."

"This is emptiness. It doesn't know of anything you talk about. It is nothing."

"This is everything. A simultaneous explosion of time and space. We are all at the same time, from every timeline, in every outcome."

"This is time. A slow, steady, ticking bomb. A horizontal feel, a frustrating feeling, a means to an end."

"This is you. The embodiment of one single breath, a speck of nothingness, a blip. Enjoy that while you are by being fully you."

Born and raised in Serbia in 1936, he was a mischievous child. He never let anything stop him from achieving his goals, and he grew up to be a successful architect.

After a long battle with cancer, his wife of many years passed. Left alone with a son, he needed a fresh start. A few months later, they moved to the beautiful tropical city of Caracas, Venezuela and started their new life.

On Wednesday, May 13, 1968, he was stopped at a red light and an older lady tried transitioning her car from one lane to another where there was clearly no room for her, somehow causing even more unnecessary stoppage in an already congested avenue. Angry that she didn't know how and where to position her car amidst the rush hour traffic, he rolled down his window and started yelling profanities at her in his native tongue.

"Jebem ti sunce, majku da ti jebem! Pa gde se sad nadje ti ovde!?"

Translation (in a milder form): "Fuck you! How the hell did you end up here!?"

He continued to yell at the poor old woman, letting out his anger. In the midst of rush hour traffic in a large city, she was bound to be used to people yelling things at her. He would have chosen to yell at her in Spanish, but since it was still quite rusty, he settled for a language she wouldn't understand.

"Vozi ajde! O jebote!" ("Drive already, fuck!"), he continued.

Waving his hands at her to move forward, she suddenly turned around toward his direction and very slowly rolled down the passenger window. Tilting her head, so she could peek out to see what all the yelling was about, he continued to gesture violently, clearly indicating he was out of patience. He needed to communicate what he needed from her somehow since language was a barrier.

Her face turned from amusement to anger as he continued yelling at her; finally, she'd had enough and yelled back:

"Pa dal se tako govori starijoj gospodji!?" ("Is that how you speak to an older lady!?")

Shocked at the words he just heard come out her mouth he sheepishly rolled up his window and proceeded to mind his own business in shame. It was just his luck, that in the middle of Caracas, during rush hour, he would yell at the only other Serbian trying to get home from work.

Goes to show you, Dad, be careful what you say and what language you say it in, you never know who your audience might be.

He searched for years to try and find the woman and apologize to her for his very rude behavior. He never found her.

I never should have gotten on this plane. Sitting beside a kid with a vendetta towards his father and a recently thirty something widowed woman is making my migraine worse. I popped a pill before we boarded, but it seems to be wearing off faster than I'd like. I figured I would at least get a nap in before landing, but it seems my wishes are futile at best.

The flight attendant seems to be having a rough day as well, so we have been telepathically commutating our grief to each other through looks.

The kid besides me is yelling at his father while the widowed woman cries for her lost companion. I turn around to comfort her by asking her to tell me her story.

"I loved her so much," she said. "But cancer eventually took her from me. I am flying to Greece where we met, so I can scatter her ashes over the ocean. She wanted to learn to fly after she died."

After we chat, she falls asleep and the kid also calms down watching an animated movie. His father relieved to be free from all the yelling shoots me an apologetic look. I nod in understanding, reassuring him I accept his sincere apology.

I stand up to go to the bathroom only to realize all of them are occupied. At least I get to stretch my legs while I wait.

"So, what's your name?"

I abruptly turn around, the flight attendant smiling at me.

"Evan." I blush.

This strange feeling of excitement rushes through my body, and I hope the flight attendant stays to continue talking to me. I haven't felt this way in a very long time. Years ago, my heart got so broken I didn't know if I was ever going to recover. For some reason, I feel it again as I talk to the flight attendant and I hope it lingers a while. I missed it.

"Nice to meet you Evan. I'm David."

Even the mouse in the corner of my closet can't seem to muster the strength to stay hidden from me, so we made a deal not to invade each other's spaces.

This concept seems easy enough, but who do you stare at when in a group of three? Seems unfair if the mouse and dog both stare at me, while I stare back at the mouse. Now no one's watching the dog. All eyes in a lot of pressure.

Sweat starts to drip down my forehead and into my left eye. I keep staring, because I can't feel a thing.

After a few minutes, my eye is drenched in sweat, but the game is too intense. I am not about to lose to a mouse and a dog. I need to up my game.

The air still circulates the room, cooling off the premises and surrounding areas. Everything becomes more breathable. I feel like I can feel my skin smiling back at me, and this is when I realize I am still in a 3-way staring competition with my two animal friends.

No one is looking at the dog. Why is no one looking at the dog? Why did I choose to stare at the mouse? Do I feel safer knowing my dog will not betray me? Am I scared my dog might eat the mouse? Why do we choose who to stare at when we choose?

So many questions I will never be able to answer as the room cools off for the first time in hours. The mouse slips back into his hole, choosing to lose this battle with dignity. As I look back at my dog, he is already fast asleep, my glass eye still soaked in sweat.

They approached the woods as the sun hid behind the clouds, one single droplet of rain falling to its demise as the wind blew it in the wrong direction.

"Stop. This doesn't feel right. I think we should turn around."

The girl looked at her boyfriend and laughed an unpleasant sort of sound that she knew made him uncomfortable.

"You want me to turn around after all the shit we've had to go through to get here? You can't be serious. Take this and help me."

He looked at the rope hanging by her bloody fingertips and sighed before taking it from her. The rain should have fallen by now, but all he felt was the roaring wind on his skin telling him to run. He took the rope and tied it around his neck.

"Now what?" he said.

"Now you start walking. Let's go. It's not far from here."

They walked a few more miles until reaching a cliff. The purple waterfall falling against the orange rocks was a sight so mesmerizing they stopped to stare for a long while. The sun came back out from behind the clouds, warming up their bloody bodies as a sign of peace.

"You still want to do this?" he asked.

"Yes."

The weather suddenly turned cold as the snow started to fall. Leaves on the trees froze over and the waterfall dried off instantaneously, completely vanishing from existence. In a matter of seconds, this world stood still as Alice and Cam took their last watery breath at the bottom of the ocean.

I am currently stuck in the center of the universe. If you want to know what that means, so do I. Both everything and nothing happens here, and no, I am not a God.

Yesterday I had a sip of coffee before the tremors started and I had to sit down to think. Doctors told me I have a few more months of normalcy before things start getting bad, but it seems to be progressing faster than expected. I'm not exactly scared, but I'm definitely angry.

My days are not fun anymore. It takes me twice as much time to get from point A to point B. I remember most of my life, but forget the simple day to day stuff. My tolerance for pointless conversations has not only diminished, but completely evaporated, and my patience in time has grown.

When I was younger, I had an affinity for bad movies. I would sit through them laughing my way to tears, only to realize the time, effort, and money spent to produce such shit. Then I would drink myself into oblivion and repeat the process the next day.

I would occasionally take walks to the park that sat beside my house, but hated the yelling children that often bounced on the trampoline. If the swings were empty, I'd occupy them by sitting still and staring at the sky, just to mess with them, teaching them important life lessons that privilege has to be earned.

My siblings all died young, with my parents, in a car accident. I was the youngest and don't remember them. Hardly a trauma. I was then raised by my mother's sister, who was a very nice woman. She never did much with her life, but never screwed it up either, so I think she died peacefully bland.

My career took away any remaining shred of childhood innocence I had left, and I spent the next 50 years working the same job. Now I am old and dying, or possibly already dead.

My life was a boring fuck of a disaster, but it was mine and so, I remember it with love.

The couch sinks into me sometimes while I watch TV. Mostly during my favorite shows, but there are times when I lack the appropriate amount of sleep and it sinks right back into my arms. I think it might be in love with me.

For the longest time I tried to understand the feeling, only to realize I wasn't going crazy. That hurts a little, because I have no one on my side to believe me. So, now that most of my friends have left me, I talk to my couch, and I think I love it too.

There are no explanations for crazy stories. I have learned to be ok with the concept of acceptance, but its practicality has never resonated. Now most people just call me sad. They aren't wrong. Most days it takes all of my energy to part from my couch, only to end up under my covers hiding from the world.

We aren't all made equally. Some of us were shipped to earth missing a few crucial parts, and now that I am out of meds all I do is cry and hope my couch will continue loving the messy existence I am.

He walked in tall. The laces on his grey shoes were bright pink, a neon color you could only find at a rave party. White pants followed shortly after the little gap of skin between his shoes and flamingo socks. A comedian. On his pockets, splotches of paint, but not enough to assume the profession. One hand tucked inside his jacket marked a quiet cool, while his other hand reached out to shake the man's who welcomed him. He had no ring on his finger, assumed single, and three wooden bracelets that hung off his hand indicating an appreciation for chic. His jacket was a distant blue color, sharing its space with colorless geometrical shapes, a clash between the straight edge and the obscure. Underneath the jacket a shirt. Simple, chaotic, yet colorful enough it caught the laziest of eyes. True surrealism in a frame of a painting, fresh enough it still dripped on the wooden floor of the gallery. He smiled, his front teeth overlapping just enough to give out a bad-boy vibe, his full lips embracing them with pride.

He turned around to observe the room. His eyes were dark and tempestuous as the center of a sunflower, bright enough they bloomed under the red chandelier above him. Turning back to take off his jacket he finally revealed his muscular arms, but he was no athlete. A single profession could not describe him, but he would burn himself into the minds of a crowd, like cows herded by a legless shepherd. His hair was thick, dark and styled. He looked approachable, a breath of fresh air among the pile of worthless dust accumulating in corners, holding their drinks, and laughing with people they would forget, regretting that last drink of the night.

"Hey, I'm Euric." He said.

He checked the torn slip of paper in his hand. The address was correct, but from the look of things, nobody was there. The house seemed abandoned, yet not fully deserted. He was in the right place. He took a few moments before curving his hand into a fist and knocking on the door. No answer. He tried again. Finally, from a distance, footsteps were heard approaching the door. They sounded sharp yet gentle, a woman in heels.

"Who is it?"

"My name is Fredrick Malone. Your friend Catharine Burk sent me."

Slowly, the door started to open. In front of him stood a tall, slim, well dressed woman in her 30s. Her hair was long and blonde, her eyes the color of a good Merlot, wearing a tight and short yellow dress. She looked stern and confused by his presence.

"Yes?"

"I, I am sorry to bother you ma'am. Catharine told me you might be able to help me."

"With?"

"My back. It's killing me."

She rolled her eyes and waived him in with her long skinny hand. As he started to enter, the wooden steps caved in and tore into his leg. He pushed himself back up, bleeding heavily. The woman continued staring at him in confusion. After a few seconds, she started walking into the house.

"Come inside. We'll fix it."

He limped into the living room and sat on the couch. It smelled old and stale, the fabric ripped off in places. The wood on the floor was heavily damaged, and the paint on the walls cracked. To his left was a coffee table that seemed out of place and to his right, a painting of a man that could be presumed the woman's husband.

"Thank you." she said.

"Excuse me?"

"Thank you for coming in. Let me get the bandages."

She walked away and left him on the couch, bleeding onto her floor. He took off his jacket to try and slow down the bleeding with no success. A few seconds later she returned with some rubbing alcohol and bandages. She placed them on the couch next to him, went down on her knees, and ripped the bottom of his jeans.

"Thank you." She said.

"Excuse me?"

"For waiting. I must have misplaced the alcohol."

She took the bottle off the couch, unscrewed the cap and poured it all on his wound. The alcohol stung, his teeth clutched together as he held back the tears. His blood mixed itself with the alcohol, flooding the floor around them. Then, she took the bandages and tightly wrapped them around the wound.

"There, all done." She said.

"Please, let me help you clean the floor. I feel awful about all of this."

"Don't worry. It will slip through the cracks right down to the basement where the rats live. They'll have a party tonight."

He wasn't sure if it was a joke or if she was serious. Studying her face, the only thing he gathered was that she had an extraordinary beauty.

"Tell me about your back."

Her statement snapped him back into the room.

"I, I have scoliosis. I fell off our ladder picking the olive tree. Haven't been able to go a day without pain since."

"When did it happen?"

"About a week ago."

She continued to stare at him. Her eyes seemed to change color.

"Yes." She said.

"What?"

"Yes, I think I can help you. Take off your shirt."

Confused but willing to oblige he stood up in pain and took off his shirt. She took it from his hands and put it on the misplaced coffee table. Her hands met his shoulders, gesturing him to sit back down.

"Where exactly does it hurt?"

"The center."

She came closer, putting one leg over him, sitting down on his knees facing him. Her hands slowly wrapped around his naked back, her fingernails penetrating his skin while her lips met his neck. Confused, his back stiffened, and his heartbeat started to rise. She slowly lifted her head, looked him in the eyes and smiled. Her legs spread further apart as her body got closer to his. In that moment, she had him locked like a statue pulling her hands towards her and snapping his back into place. She stood up and walked towards the kitchen.

"Tell Catharine I say hello. She was a dear friend."

He stood up and found his shirt and jacket. Unsure how to feel, he got dressed and thanked the woman for her help. His pain was gone, but he felt oddly abused non the less. He liked but feared her. As he started walking toward the door, he caught another glimpse of the painting on the wall. It changed. Staring back at him was a face much too familiar. A face he woke up to every morning. A face he wanted to betray with the woman standing behind him. Catharine.

Chills ran down my back almost as if to signal me a warning. I came here for a reason, and this time, I wasn't going to leave without her. The blue lace starting at the fingertips, intertwined at her middle finger, a fuck you to my bank account. I could afford her this time, and she would soon be mine.

She was the silent type. Long and curly, but with substance. There was a story to her I ached to know, and as those sweet seconds passed by while I stood there and stared, my lips salivated like a dog's before dinner. I wanted her, and only her.

The air around me felt stale, suffocating my mind from thinking clearly. I wished there was a window I could open to air out the room, but I was afraid to leave her sight. If she ended up with someone else, my heart would be forever broken, and my ego would follow.

My thoughts continued to talk to me as I stood there admiring her elegance. A man passed by me, nudging me ever so slightly with his shoulder as if to make sure I knew he existed. I didn't care for him. Another man passed by me a few minutes later, also nudging me with his shoulder. I didn't care for him either. When the third man came along nudging me with his shoulder, I started sensing a pattern. A fourth would follow. Somebody was trying to move me from my position in the most uncomfortable way. I didn't care.

My credit card was safe at home in my dresser. Today was a day where I paid cash, in full. The air was getting dryer, my thoughts getting quieter as the room got louder. I couldn't look away from her. She was my prize and I was winning tonight. No one could distract me from what I wanted.

Another nudge shifted me from my position. Then another one. Three more followed. I still didn't care. Too distracted by her beauty, I started stripping her. She was everything. By now, I've waited too long to undress her from the plastic shell of the human she hung of. Her color was sky blue, peaceful, yet daring. Handmade, she was one of a kind, with lace and silk working together as one. The pearls on the collar were a necessary touch, and she sparkled vibrantly, almost unrealistically. A tint of yellow and orange mixed themselves with the blue, details I missed while mesmerized by her.

Suddenly from the corner of my eye I saw something. I felt as if someone was watching me undress her, and I felt uncomfortably hot. I cared this time, a protective instinct flushed over me like a mother wolf taking care of her young. No one was taking her from me today, and for the first time, I looked up since entering the room. It was on fire.

I turned back to her, this time not taking my time. I tore the rest of her off without damaging a single stitch. It was getting hotter and the sweat on my forehead met my eyes. People were running passed me, trying to find their way to the exit. I needed to cash out, throwing my money towards a direction that seemed most likely to take it. She was hard earned and the flames weren't going to stop me from paying my dues. I ran for the door but tripped and fell, a hand reaching out for mine to help me stand back up. He was a handsome, tall, dark fella.

"You need to move! This building won't last long. Please, let me carry you out."

Suddenly I felt lifted from the ground, the room foggy from the smoke, my thoughts a high pitched buzz. I started to cough, my hands wrapped around his neck feeling the turbulence as we ran to safety. We made it out of the building just in time before it collapsed into a pile of burned brick. He let go of me and placed me back on my feet, the fresh air a refreshing smell. He really was very handsome, but I had no time for him. I thanked him for saving my life and rushed to tend to her. She meant more to me than him, been in my thoughts longer, I dreamt about her often. I wanted to enjoy her in all her beauty, and celebrate our new journey together. Finally, I had her, after all this time. I brought my hands up to smell her, feel her on my skin, see her in sunlight, but my hands were empty and grey. I still remember hearing my heart crack as I realized she was burnt into ashes under the charred mausoleum of a building, still whispering my name.

It was very confusing, and it was New Year's. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. He was nowhere to be found. I searched for a while and found him in the embrace of another man giving away what was supposed to be my first kiss of the year. Betrayed, I let them continue their fun, pretending as though their act just ricocheted off me. The snow outside melted before it hit the ground, the pasta boiling on the stove was 20 minutes overcooked, and a few of my friends were passed out on the floor after playing King's cup. The clock continued ticking, it was suddenly 5am. Where was he again? He wasn't in bed, he wasn't by the pool, or in any of the bathrooms. Searching through time and space for what seemed like an endless adventure, I finally found him in the corner room of the house. With him. They were sitting next to the old Windows 98 computer, the light off the screen reflecting onto their lying faces.

"We need to talk about this." I said.

"Who are you?" said the other kid.

"I'm his girlfriend"

His face flushed with an apple shade of red, and I understood in that moment the information he just learned was new to him. The boyfriend wasn't telling him the whole truth. My first instinct was to feel sorry for the kid, but after a few seconds I just felt close to him. I knew we would be great friends. I liked him. Panicking, the kid took my hand and sat me on his lap across the betrayer.

"I'm so sorry. I had no idea." said the kid.

"I caught that."

"Please know, I would never do anything like that if I knew!"

"My beef is with him honey, not you."

"I don't know what to do! How can I fix this? I'd like to fix this!"

I was going to respond with a cool but cold "Don't worry about it", but as I started getting it out the kid wrapped his fingers around my hair, pulled me toward him, and kissed me. There was tongue, it was long, and it was good. What the hell was happening? I let it go on for too long, so I pulled away and stood up in a hurry.

"What the fuck?" I asked.

"I'm sorry! I panicked!"

"So, you decided to kiss me?"

"I didn't know what to do."

"He is a good kisser isn't he?" the boyfriend chipped in.

All of a sudden, I was pulled in by both of them, with nowhere to run and nowhere to hide. I liked it. Challenges intrigue me. My boyfriend's lips finally met mine for the first time that night.
